In the 1940s, Pasley wrote in her cookie
book that “since the stuffs that cookies are
made of come from the ends of the Seven
Seas, you shouldn’t expect to be able to buy
them all in one store.” Like many cookbooks
of that era, she offered suggestions for
where one could obtain more challenging
items. (The most unexpected ingredient
uncovered in the holiday cookbook
collection? The salty star of Prannie
Rhatigan’s “Irish Seaweed Christmas
Kitchen.”)
